methodological_rigor.justification: Comprehensive mechanistic study combining in vitro cell biology, in vivo xenograft models, and clinical sample analysis. Multiple independent breast cancer cell lines tested with TSPAN13 knockdown/knockout approaches. Proper controls (TSPAN13-WT vs. deficient) and vehicle controls in in vivo experiments. Statistical testing with P-values reported. In vivo experiments with n=5-8 mice per group. Clinical sample correlational analysis with CD8+ infiltration. Flow cytometry and functional CD8+ T-cell killing assays properly designed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case-control clinical study combined with mechanistic validation demonstrating TSPAN13 as immune evasion mechanism in 'cold' breast cancer tumors. TSPAN13 expression inversely correlates with CD8+ T-cell infiltration in patient samples. Identifies actionable target (TSPAN13) whose loss enhances MHC-I presentation and CD8+ T-cell recognition. Shows sensitization to anti-PD-L1 therapy through TSPAN13 inhibition. Direct relevance to immunotherapy resistance in breast cancer.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive methods for cell culture, genetic engineering (CRISPR), immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, in vivo tumor models, and clinical sample analysis. ARRIVE compliance for animal studies evident. Ethics approvals referenced. Patient sample source and informed consent mentioned. However, no explicit raw data or code deposition statement. Some supplementary methods likely more comprehensive than main manuscript.

novelty_literature.justification: Identifies TSPAN13 as novel regulator of MHC-I surface expression through ubiquitin-mediated degradation. Mechanism showing TSPAN13-STIP1 interaction promoting lysosomal targeting is new. Connects tetraspanin biology to immune evasion, expanding understanding of cold tumor biology. Demonstrates therapeutic vulnerability in breast cancer immunotherapy resistance. Significant mechanistic contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript with clear introduction to cold tumor biology and immune checkpoint inhibitor resistance. Methods comprehensively described. Results logically progress from mechanistic discovery through functional validation to clinical correlation. Figures effectively communicate TSPAN13 effects on MHC-I, CD8+ T-cell activation, and therapeutic sensitivity. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within breast cancer immunotherapy landscape.

key_strengths: Identifies TSPAN13 as novel immune checkpoint regulator: promotes MHC-I degradation to evade CD8+ T-cell recognition
Mechanistic clarity: TSPAN13 recruits STIP1 to ubiquitinate MHC-I, promoting lysosomal degradation; TSPAN13 loss restores MHC-I surface expression
Clinical relevance demonstrated: TSPAN13 expression inversely correlates with CD8+ infiltration in patient samples; TSPAN13 loss enhances anti-PD-L1 efficacy
Comprehensive validation: in vitro mechanisms, in vivo xenografts, clinical correlations, and functional CD8+ T-cell killing assays all support findings
key_concerns: Limited to triple-negative breast cancer xenografts; applicability to other breast cancer subtypes (luminal, HER2+) not addressed
Clinical cohort analysis correlational only; no prospective validation of TSPAN13 as predictor of immunotherapy response
Therapeutic development pathway unclear; TSPAN13 is not easily druggable target; small-molecule or biologic strategies not discussed
Patient sample size for correlation analysis not explicitly stated; statistical power of clinical association not reported
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 2 paper: strong mechanistic immunology work with clear clinical relevance to breast cancer immunotherapy resistance. Requires larger clinical validation cohort and therapeutic development strategy. Appropriate for high-impact cancer immunology journal; represents actionable discovery.
